title: Apparel & Accessories Ecommerce Benchmarks for 2026
summary: Explore the AOV, conversion rate, and bounce rate data relevant to brands within the Apparel & Accessories category of ecommerce for 2026.
body_markdown:
## AOV Holds Up While CVR Slips and Bounce Rate Climbs


The benchmarks:[1.76% median conversion rate](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-conversion-rate) ,[$429 median AOV](https://getshogun.com/benchmarks/ecommerce-average-order-value) . The 25th–75th percentile AOV range is $239–$834. Conversion and engagement are both down against 2025, but AOV is up: same-store matched AOV is 3.0% higher year over year.


Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date Ecommerce Benchmark Reports (January–September 2026), Apparel & Accessories.


2026 has been a more challenging year for Apparel & Accessories than 2025 — though the picture depends on which metric you look at.


On conversion: every month from January through September 2026 came in below the same month of 2025, and Q3 didn’t deliver the seasonal lift it did last year. Among stores active in both quarters, CVR fell 5.5% from Q2 to Q3 2026, compared with a 10.8% rise over the same quarters in 2025.


Bounce rates have been climbing in parallel, rising from 36–38% in early 2025 to 44–49% in Q3 2026, with August (48.9%) the high point. More visitors are leaving quickly than in the same period of 2025.


On order value: the opposite. On a matched same-store basis, median AOV is up 3.0% year over year, and it held steady from Q2 to Q3 (+0.6%). Monthly median AOV recovered from its December dip ($355) and reached $431 in September 2026, the highest point in the trend window.


> *CVR and AOV are moving in opposite directions. Fewer sessions are converting, but the ones that do are producing larger baskets.*


For context: Apparel & Accessories’ 1.76% CVR places it in the middle of the 10-industry benchmark — above Home & Garden and Consumer Electronics, but well below the repeat-purchase categories like Health & Wellness, Beauty & Personal Care and Food & Beverage. Its $429 median AOV is the fourth-highest of the 11 categories we track, which makes Apparel & Accessories more of a considered purchase than its conversion rate alone suggests.


## Conversion Rate Benchmark: 2026 Year to Date


The median Apparel & Accessories conversion rate from January through September 2026 was 1.76%, placing it in the middle tier of the 10 published industries — sixth, just below Business & Industrial (1.80%) and just above Home & Garden (1.65%).


n=803 active Shopify stores, January–September 2026. Stores with CVR below 0.1% or above 25% excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date CVR Benchmark Report.


Apparel & Accessories’ mid-table CVR paired with a $429 median AOV — fourth-highest in the dataset — is an unusual combination. Shoppers arrive engaged and browse extensively before buying, so the category doesn’t fit neatly into either the repeat-purchase group (high CVR, lower AOV) or the considered-purchase group (higher AOV, lower CVR).


> *Apparel & Accessories’ bounce rate of 44.1% (January–September 2026) is the third-lowest of any category in the dataset. Low CVR here is less a traffic-quality problem than a reflection of a category that takes more consideration before purchase — though bounce rate has been rising.*


## **CVR & Bounce Rates Trending in Wrong Direction: January 2025 through September 2026**


The graph below shows monthly median CVR and bounce rate for active Apparel & Accessories stores in Shogun’s conversion tracking network. Twenty-one months of data makes the 2026 shift visible against a full year of 2025 baseline.


n=126–174 active stores per month. Each month measured on its own; CVR filter 0.1%–25% per site per month. Source: Shogun session and conversion tracking, Apparel & Accessories.


CVR ran in the 1.81%–2.49% range across every month of 2025, with a peak in November. Through 2026 it has held in a lower 1.68%–2.03% band.


**Every month of 2026 so far has come in below the same month of 2025.**


Bounce rate has been climbing steadily — from about 36% in spring 2025 to 44–49% in Q3 2026, roughly 7–11 percentage points above Q3 2025. As fewer sessions convert, more visitors are leaving from the first page.


## Average Order Value Benchmark: 2026 Year to Date


The 2026 year-to-date median AOV for Apparel & Accessories was $429, based on full-store Shopify order data across 656 qualifying stores. This data set is separate from the CVR cohort above and uses different qualifying criteria.


January–September 2026, n=656 stores with at least 375 orders; AOV above $5,000 excluded. Source: Shogun 2026 Year-to-Date AOV Benchmark Report, Apparel & Accessories.


## AOV Trending Up — June 2025 through September 2026


The graph below tracks monthly median AOV for Apparel & Accessories stores, with each month measured on its own (544–673 stores per month). The trend starts in June 2025 because store coverage in the order data was much thinner before then.


n=544–673 stores per month; each month measured on its own (stores with at least 50 orders that month, AOV $1–$5,000). Source: Shogun AOV benchmark data, Apparel & Accessories.


AOV climbed through 2025, reaching $413 in October and $410 in November before a sharp dip to $355 in December — likely the effect of holiday promotions and clearance. It has climbed through 2026 since, reaching $431 in September, the high point of the 16-month window. On a matched same-store basis, median AOV is up 3.0% year over year.


## AOV and CVR Are Moving in Opposite Directions


AOV is up while CVR is down. The buyer pool seems to be narrowing toward higher intent shoppers, while fringe buyers fall off.


Look at both trends side by side and a clear pattern emerges: conversion is getting harder to earn in Apparel, but the transactions that do happen are worth more.


On a matched same-store basis (n=495 stores active in both January–September 2025 and January–September 2026), median AOV grew from $417 to $429 — a +3.0% year-over-year increase. Over the same period, every month of 2026 converted below the same month of 2025.


One interpretation: the pool of buyers is narrowing toward more deliberate, higher-intent shoppers. Casual browsers are leaving faster — bounce rate in Q3 2026 ran 7–11 points above Q3 2025 — while the visitors who do convert are spending more.


## A Note on Sub-Markets Within Apparel & Accessories


The $429 median is a useful reference point, but the P25-to-P75 range tells an equally important story. The middle 50% of Apparel & Accessories stores in this dataset have an AOV somewhere between $239 and $834. That’s a $595 spread within a single category benchmark.


That range reflects how different the sub-markets within Apparel & Accessories are. A fast-fashion retailer averaging around $40 per order and a premium outerwear brand above $600 are both counted in the same category. Conversion varies for similar reasons: a $35 t-shirt and a $450 coat involve very different buying decisions.


> *The $429 median is a benchmark for Apparel & Accessories as a category. Your relevant benchmark is the sub-market you actually compete in — which may sit well above or below the median.*


If your AOV is well below $239 or above $834, you’re operating outside the category’s typical distribution, and the median is only a loose comparison. The trend signals — conversion trailing 2025, bounce rate rising, AOV up year over year — are likely more actionable than where the median sits.
